description: Loading config.json and saving it again: what the next save writes, and whether the file is copied to config.pre-profiles.json first. The file is read as Swift's JSONDecoder reads it. The document must scan: UTF-8 (one optional BOM skipped) or UTF-16/UTF-32 detected from a BOM or the zero bytes, space, tab, LF and CR around tokens, at most 512 open containers, one trailing comma allowed, keys unescaped strictly at scan time, and an object root; otherwise the file is corrupt (saved is null: the app moves it to config.json.bak and runs on the defaults). Values are converted only when a known key reads them, so a malformed number or string fails that one field, which takes its default; of two equal keys the first wins. Each known key reads tolerantly: null or a wrong type is the default; optional strings read empty as absent; summaryModel is trimmed of whitespacesAndNewlines and falls back to haiku when blank; harnessKind, acpAgent, controlMode and remoteTargetKind must be exactly one of their listed values; listenerPort must be 1...65535 (else 48738); maxSpokenChars and listenerPort are Swift Ints (an exactly integral decimal reads, its double must lie in Int's range), ttsRate a Float (a nonzero value that rounds to zero or past Float.max fails), arrays and dictionaries of strings all or nothing. The mapping subtree (deviceMappings, the legacy mapping) loads as mapping/config-load.json pins, and decides backupBeforeSave. The save is JSONEncoder with .prettyPrinted and .sortedKeys: keys in Unicode scalar order, two-space indent, "key" : value, empty containers as an open and close bracket around a blank line, / escaped as \/, nil optionals left out, no trailing newline; a Float is written with its shortest digits, exponential below 1e-4 or above 2^24. Unknown keys are never written.
function: ConfigStore load and save (AppConfig decoding, the pre-profiles backup decision, ConfigStore.encode) — input the file's bytes (a string, or {"hex": <bytes>}), expected {saved, backupBeforeSave}: saved is the text the next save writes as a list of lines joined with "\n" (no trailing newline), or null when the file is corrupt; backupBeforeSave is whether config.pre-profiles.json is written first (false for a corrupt file)
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v2.4 B and C, v2.14; Tests/PowerUpTests/ConfigFixtureTests.swift testConfigRoundTripTable loads the input as the app does, encodes it with ConfigStore.encode and compares the bytes, and writes the input to a temporary config.json, runs ConfigStore.backupConfigBeforeLossyLoadIfNeeded and checks that config.pre-profiles.json exists exactly when backupBeforeSave is true. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/config.rs config_round_trip_cases runs config::load_config on the bytes and config::encode_config on the result and compares the lines.
capturedAgainst: Swift 5.9.2 JSONDecoder and JSONEncoder (Xcode 15.2) on macOS 27.2, PowerUp at 46239df

cases.name: null values read as the defaults
cases.reason: decodeIfPresent reads null as absent, so a null is the default, never a failure.

cases.name: every optional key set
cases.reason: Every optional key is written when set, each in its sorted place.

cases.name: empty optional strings are left out
cases.reason: An empty optional string reads as nil and is not written; an empty controllerDeviceID is Automatic, never a pin (HK-018, HK-158).

cases.name: a blank optional string is kept
cases.reason: Only an empty string reads as nil; whitespace is not trimmed from optional strings.

cases.reason: An empty array is a value, written as [ ] over a blank line by the pretty printer.

cases.reason: An element whose escape is invalid fails its array, not the file.

cases.reason: A wrong type gives the empty default.

cases.reason: JSONDecoder keeps the first of two equal keys in a nested dictionary too.

cases.name: sessionIDsByProject keys are written in scalar order
cases.reason: Sorted keys order by Unicode scalar (byte order): space before slash, digits by character, upper case before underscore before lower case, é after z.

cases.name: a decomposed key sorts by its scalars
cases.reason: No normalization: e followed by U+0301 sorts after ex and before f.

cases.name: an unknown control mode and target kind fall back
cases.reason: A fixed-vocabulary setting with an unknown value reads as its default (HK-156).

cases.name: the vocabulary is matched exactly
cases.reason: No case folding or trimming: ACP, Remote and a padded agent are unknown values.

cases.name: known vocabulary values are kept
cases.reason: Every listed value is kept as written.

cases.name: the other vocabulary values are kept
cases.reason: claudeBridge and frontmost are listed values.

cases.name: a custom agent keeps its command
cases.reason: The custom command is a plain string, not trimmed.

cases.name: plain strings are not checked
cases.reason: Only the four fixed vocabularies are checked; other strings are kept verbatim, even empty.

cases.name: a blank summaryModel reads as haiku
cases.reason: A blank alias must never reach the CLI argv (HK-158).

cases.name: summaryModel is trimmed
cases.reason: Whitespace and newlines around the alias are trimmed before it is kept.

cases.name: summaryModel trims every Unicode space
cases.reason: Foundation's whitespacesAndNewlines includes U+200B, U+3000, NEL and the paragraph separator.

cases.name: the first of two equal top-level keys wins
cases.reason: JSONDecoder keeps the first of two equal keys.

cases.name: trailing commas are accepted
cases.reason: JSONDecoder accepts one trailing comma in an object or array.

cases.name: a UTF-8 byte order mark is skipped
cases.reason: A file saved by an editor that writes a BOM must still load.

cases.name: UTF-16LE without a byte order mark loads
cases.reason: JSONDecoder detects UTF-16 from the zero bytes; the save writes UTF-8.

cases.name: UTF-16BE without a byte order mark loads
cases.reason: Big-endian UTF-16 is detected the same way.

cases.name: UTF-16LE with a byte order mark loads
cases.reason: A UTF-16 BOM selects the encoding.

cases.name: UTF-16BE with a byte order mark loads
cases.reason: A big-endian BOM selects the encoding.

cases.name: UTF-32BE without a byte order mark loads
cases.reason: Three leading zero bytes mean UTF-32BE.

cases.name: UTF-32LE without a byte order mark loads
cases.reason: Three trailing zero bytes after the first mean UTF-32LE.

cases.name: UTF-32LE with a byte order mark is corrupt
cases.reason: FF FE is taken as UTF-16LE, which then starts with U+0000 and fails: the file is moved aside (a Foundation quirk the core keeps).

cases.name: a malformed number in an unknown key is ignored
cases.reason: JSONDecoder only checks a number's grammar when a field reads it; an unknown key never is.

cases.name: an overflowing number in an unknown key is ignored
cases.reason: The overflow is found only when a field reads the number.

cases.name: a bad escape in an unknown key is ignored
cases.reason: A string's escapes are checked only when a field reads it.

cases.name: a bad escape fails only its field
cases.reason: The other fields still load; model reads as the default.

cases.name: a raw tab fails only its field
cases.reason: A raw control character fails the string, not the file.

cases.name: an unpaired surrogate fails only its field
cases.reason: An unpaired surrogate escape fails the string, not the file.

cases.name: invalid UTF-8 fails only its field
cases.reason: A stray byte inside a string fails that string, not the file.

cases.name: a stray A9 byte fails only its field
cases.reason: JSONDecoder does not share JSONSerialization's U+FFFD reading of 0xA9.

cases.name: invalid UTF-8 in an unknown key's value is ignored
cases.reason: An unread string is never checked.

cases.name: a leading U+FEFF in a string is kept
cases.reason: JSONDecoder keeps a string's leading U+FEFF (JSONSerialization would drop it).

cases.name: an escaped U+0000 is an ordinary character
cases.reason: \u0000 is allowed and written back as \u0000.

cases.name: an escaped key reads as its text
cases.reason: Keys are unescaped, so an escaped spelling names the same key.

cases.name: a bad key in a nested object is ignored
cases.reason: Only the root's keys are converted when the file is read; a nested object's keys are converted when a field reads that object, and nothing reads an unknown key.

cases.name: a bad key fails sessionIDsByProject as a whole
cases.reason: Reading the dictionary converts every key; one that does not convert gives the empty default.

cases.name: a bad key drops the profile holding it
cases.reason: The mapping subtree reads a profile with a key that does not convert as null, so that profile is dropped and the file is copied first.

cases.name: whitespace around the root is allowed
cases.reason: Space, tab, LF and CR may surround the root.

cases.name: invalid UTF-8 in a key is corrupt
cases.reason: Keys are converted when the file is scanned, so a bad key fails the whole file.

cases.name: a bad escape in a key is corrupt
cases.reason: A key's escapes are checked at scan time.

cases.name: an array root is corrupt
cases.reason: The root must be an object.

cases.name: a string root is corrupt
cases.reason: The root must be an object.

cases.name: a null root is corrupt
cases.reason: The root must be an object.

cases.name: an empty file is corrupt
cases.reason: No JSON at all is corrupt: the file is moved aside and the app runs on defaults (HK-160).

cases.name: a blank file is corrupt
cases.reason: Whitespace alone is no document.

cases.name: garbage after the root is corrupt
cases.reason: Nothing but whitespace may follow the root.

cases.name: NaN is corrupt
cases.reason: NaN is not JSON; the scan fails the file.

cases.name: a number running into a letter is corrupt
cases.reason: A number must end at a structural character, whitespace or the end.

cases.name: an unterminated object is corrupt
cases.reason: A truncated file is corrupt.

cases.name: a form feed before the root is corrupt
cases.reason: Only space, tab, LF and CR count as whitespace.

cases.name: two commas are corrupt
cases.reason: Only one trailing comma is accepted, never an empty member.

cases.name: a comment is corrupt
cases.reason: JSON has no comments.

cases.name: a single-quoted string is corrupt
cases.reason: Strings take double quotes.

cases.name: 512 open containers load
cases.reason: JSONDecoder reads 512 levels of nesting; the approve action keeps its unknown sibling and the file is not copied (the HK-014 quirk).

cases.name: 513 open containers are corrupt
cases.reason: One level more fails the scan, so the file is moved aside.

cases.name: a legacy mapping migrates and asks for a backup
cases.reason: The pre-ADR-0006 mapping migrates into the DualSense profile and the file is copied before the save rewrites it (HK-014).

cases.name: a lossy deviceMappings asks for a backup
cases.reason: A binding this build cannot read is dropped, so the file is copied first.

cases.name: an empty deviceMappings is written as an empty object
cases.reason: No bindings at all is a value; the pretty printer writes { } over a blank line, and nothing is copied.

cases.name: a lazily invalid prompt drops its binding
cases.reason: The prompt cannot be read, so that binding reads as null and is dropped, and the file is copied first.

cases.name: two equal bindings keep the first
cases.reason: The mapping subtree keeps the first of two equal keys like every other object.

cases.name: a null deviceMappings gives the defaults and a backup

saved: "_0" : "Commit the current changes with a good message"
"_0" : "Run the tests and report the results"

cases.reason: A present but unreadable deviceMappings asks for the copy and runs on the defaults.

cases.name: unknown top-level keys are not saved
cases.reason: Only the known keys survive a load, so the next save drops a key this build does not know.

cases.name: a numeric action payload sibling is dropped on save
cases.reason: An action with an unknown sibling reads and saves without it; the prompt's slash is escaped.

cases.name: strings are escaped as JSONEncoder escapes them
cases.reason: Quote, backslash, slash and the C0 controls are escaped (lowercase \u00xx); DEL, U+2028, U+2029 and all other non-ASCII are written raw.

cases.name: non-ASCII paths are written raw
cases.reason: Paths are written as UTF-8 with only their slashes escaped.
